units.en: His uncles Wang Dun and Wang Dao thought the world of him.
units.literal: He was deeply esteemed by his paternal uncles Dun and Dao.

units.zh: 祖正，尚書郎。
units.en: His grandfather Wang Zheng had served as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: His grandfather Zheng was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 父曠，淮南太守。
units.en: His father Wang Kuang was the Administrator of Huainan commandery.
units.literal: His father Kuang was Administrator of Huainan.

units.zh: 訪之，乃羲之也，遂以女妻之。
units.en: They asked who he was: it was Wang Xizhi, and Xi Jian gave him his daughter in marriage.
units.literal: They inquired; it was Xizhi, and so they gave him their daughter as wife.

units.zh: 自兒娶女嫁，便懷尚子平之志，數與親知言之，非一日也。
units.en: Ever since my sons married and my daughters were given away, I have nursed the wish, like Shang Ziping of old, to leave public life; I have said as much to family and friends again and again, and not just yesterday.
units.literal: From when sons married and daughters wed, I then cherished the ambition of Shang Ziping, and several times spoke of it to kin and friends; it is not one day.

units.zh: 羲之既少有美譽，朝廷公卿皆愛其才器，頻召為侍中、吏部尚書，皆不就。
units.en: Wang Xizhi had been celebrated since his early years, and the great officers at court prized his gifts; they called him repeatedly to serve as Palace Attendant and as Minister of Personnel, but he declined every appointment.
units.literal: Xizhi, having from youth enjoyed a fine reputation, was loved by the court dukes and ministers for his talent and capacity; he was repeatedly summoned as Palace Attendant and Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, but in each case did not take office.

units.zh: 復授護軍將軍，又推遷不拜。
units.en: He was offered the post of General Who Guards the Army and once more put it off without assuming the commission.
units.literal: He was again appointed General Who Guards the Army, and again deferred and did not accept.

units.zh: 年十三，嘗謁周顗，顗察而異之。
units.en: At thirteen he paid a call on Zhou Yi, who sized him up and saw something uncommon in him.
units.literal: At age thirteen he once visited Zhou Yi; Yi observed him and considered him unusual.

units.zh: 時重牛心炙，坐客未啖，顗先割啖羲之，於是始知名。
units.en: Ox-heart roast was then considered a great delicacy. Before the other guests had tasted it, Zhou Yi carved a portion and offered it to Wang Xizhi, and only then did the boy begin to make a name for himself.
units.literal: At the time ox-heart roast was prized; the seated guests had not yet eaten when Yi first carved and fed Xizhi, and from this he first became known.

units.zh: 時太尉郗鑒使門生求女婿于導，導令就東廂遍觀子弟。
units.en: Grand Commandant Xi Jian dispatched a disciple to ask Wang Dao for a son-in-law, and Wang Dao had the man go to the eastern wing and look over every young kinsman present.
units.literal: At the time Grand Commandant Xi Jian sent a student to seek a son-in-law from Dao; Dao ordered him to go to the east wing and survey all the young men.

units.zh: 惟一人在東床坦腹食，獨若不聞。」
units.en: Only one sat on the eastern couch with his shirt open, eating unconcernedly as though nothing had happened."
units.literal: Only one man on the eastern couch ate with belly bared, alone as if he had not heard."

units.zh: 羲之遂報書曰：「吾素自無廊廟志，直王丞相時果欲內吾，誓不許之，手跡猶存，由來尚矣，不於足下參政而方進退。
units.en: Wang Xizhi answered: "I have never aspired to high ministerial rank. When Chancellor Wang once tried to bring me into the administration, I swore I would not go—the letter he wrote me is still in my keeping, and my resolve has been clear for years. I am not only now, as you take power, deciding whether to step forward or back.
units.literal: Xizhi then replied with a letter saying, "I have from of old had no ambition for the court; when Chancellor Wang truly wished to bring me in, I swore not to permit it; the handwriting still exists, it has been long thus; it is not at your entering government that I then advance or retreat.

units.zh: 若蒙驅使，關隴、巴蜀皆所不辭。
units.en: If I am ordered on a mission, I would not refuse even the road to Guanzhong, Longyou, or the Ba–Shu region.
units.literal: If I receive orders to be dispatched, Guan, Long, Ba, and Shu I all do not decline.

units.zh: 吾雖無專對之能，直謹守時命，宣國家威德，固當不同於凡使，必令遠近咸知朝廷留心於無外，此所益殊不同居護軍也。
units.en: I may lack the eloquence of a seasoned negotiator, but if I simply obey the court's commission and make known its majesty and benevolence, I can still do more than the usual envoy: I would show every quarter that the throne cares for the world beyond our borders. That service would be far more useful than warming a seat as General Who Guards the Army.
units.literal: Although I lack the ability for special diplomatic replies, simply strictly keeping timely orders and proclaiming the state's awe-inspiring virtue, solidly ought to differ from ordinary envoys, necessarily causing far and near all to know the court attends to what is beyond the borders; this benefit is extremely different from occupying Guarding the Army.

units.zh: 漢末使太傅馬日磾慰撫關東，若不以吾輕微，無所為疑，宜及初冬以行，吾惟恭以待命。」
units.en: At the end of the Han the court sent Grand Tutor Ma Midi east of the passes on a mission of consolation. If my low rank does not disqualify me, and you have no misgivings, I should leave in early winter. I await your command with all deference."
units.literal: At the end of Han they sent Grand Tutor Ma Midi to comfort and pacify Guandong; if you do not because I am slight have what to doubt, it is fitting to go by early winter; I only respectfully await orders."

units.zh: 復圖再舉，又遺浩書曰：
units.en: When Yin plotted a second offensive, Wang Xizhi wrote to him again:
units.literal: Again planning a second undertaking, he again sent Hao a letter saying:

units.zh: 知安西敗喪，公私惋怛，不能須臾去懷，以區區江左，所營綜如此，天下寒心，固以久矣，而加之敗喪，此可熟念。
units.en: The news of the defeat of the army under the General of the West has left everyone, official and commoner alike, heartsick; the sorrow will not lift. Our modest foothold south of the Yangzi has been governed to this pass; the empire has long been disheartened, and now this rout on top of everything—think hard about what that means.
units.literal: Knowing the General of the West's defeat and loss, public and private are grieved; unable for a moment to leave it from the breast—with the petty Jiangzuo, what is managed and brought together is thus; the realm's hearts are cold, solidly it has been long, and adding defeat and loss, this can be pondered maturely.

units.zh: 往事豈復可追，顧思弘將來，令天下寄命有所，自隆中興之業。
units.en: The past cannot be undone. Look instead to the future: give the people something solid to live for, and you will yourself enlarge the work of restoring the dynasty.
units.literal: Past affairs how again can be pursued; look to thinking broadly the future, causing the realm to entrust life to have a place, from this raising the enterprise of restoration.

units.zh: 政以道勝寬和為本，力爭武功，作非所當，因循所長，以固大業，想識其由來也。
units.en: Good rule rests on moral ascendancy and a calm, generous temper; to strain after military glory when the time is wrong is a mistake. Play to your strengths and shore up the great enterprise—you know this as well as I.
units.literal: Government takes the Way's victory and lenient harmony as root; striving forcefully for military merit, acting not what is appropriate, following what is long in one, to solidify the great enterprise—I suppose you recognize whence it comes.

units.zh: 自寇亂以來，處內外之任者，未有深謀遠慮，括囊至計，而疲竭根本，各從所志，竟無一功可論，一事可記，忠言嘉謀棄而莫用，遂令天下將有土崩之勢，何能不痛心悲慨也。
units.en: Since the rebellions began, those who have held office at court and on the borders have shown neither foresight nor a coherent strategy. They have drained the state's foundations while each pursued private aims, and not a single success or memorable deed has come of it. Sound counsel is thrown aside, and the empire now teeters toward collapse—how can we not feel bitter grief?
units.literal: Since the bandit turmoil, those occupying inner and outer responsibilities have not had deep plans and far considerations, tying the bag's utmost schemes, but exhausted the root, each following their ambitions; in the end not one merit can be discussed, not one affair can be recorded; loyal words and fine plans are discarded and not used, thus causing the realm about to have the momentum of landslide—how can one not be pained in heart and grieved!

units.zh: 任其事者，豈得辭四海之責！
units.en: Those who bear this burden cannot escape accountability to the whole realm.
units.literal: Those entrusted with these affairs, how can they decline responsibility for the four seas!

units.zh: 追咎往事，亦何所復及，宜更虛己求賢，當與有識共之，不可復令忠允之言常屈於當權。
units.en: Recriminations over the past accomplish nothing. Humble yourself, seek out able men, and work with those who see clearly; do not let honest advice be silenced again by whoever happens to hold power.
units.literal: Pursuing blame for past affairs, again what is there to reach; it is fitting further to empty self and seek the worthy, ought to share with those who have insight; it cannot again cause loyal and candid words constantly to be bent under those in power.

units.zh: 今軍破於外，資竭於內，保淮之志非復所及，莫過還保長江，都督將各復舊鎮，自長江以外，羈縻而已。
units.en: The field armies are shattered and the treasury is empty; we can no longer dream of holding the Huai line. The best we can do is fall back to the Yangzi, send each commander to his old post, and treat everything beyond the river as ground we merely influence at a distance.
units.literal: Now the army is broken outside, resources exhausted inside; the ambition to hold the Huai is no longer reachable; nothing surpasses returning to guard the Yangzi; supervising generals each restore old garrisons; from beyond the Yangzi, loose rein only.

units.zh: 任國鈞者，引咎責躬，深自貶降以謝百姓。
units.en: The chief ministers must own their faults, humble themselves, and make amends to the people.
units.literal: Those who bear the state's weight should draw blame and blame the self, deeply self-demote to apologize to the hundred surnames.

units.zh: 更與朝賢思布平政，除其煩苛，省其賦役，與百姓更始。
units.en: Then join the worthy men at court in planning honest administration: strip away oppressive regulations, lighten taxes and labor service, and give the common people a fresh start.
units.literal: Further with court worthies think to spread level government, remove their vexatious harshness, reduce their levies and corvée, with the hundred surnames make a new beginning.

units.zh: 庶可以允塞群望，救倒懸之急。
units.en: Only thus can you answer what the country expects of you and ease the desperate straits we are in.
units.literal: Perhaps thereby can satisfy and block the multitude's hopes, rescue the urgency of inverted hanging.

units.zh: 使君起于布衣，任天下之重，尚德之舉，未能事事允稱。
units.en: You began as a commoner and now shoulder the fate of the empire; even the best intentions cannot make every deed meet everyone's praise.
units.literal: The envoy lord rose from plain cloth, bearing the heaviness of the realm; the promotion of virtue's undertaking has not been able in every affair to be fittingly praised.

units.zh: 當董統之任而敗喪至此，恐闔朝群賢未有與人分其謗者。
units.en: Entrusted with supreme command, you have brought us to this disaster; I doubt anyone else at court will step forward to share the blame with you.
units.literal: When bearing the duty of supervising and unifying yet defeat and loss reach here, I fear the whole court's group of worthies has none who share with others their slander.

units.zh: 今亟修德補闕，廣延群賢，與之分任，尚未知獲濟所期。
units.en: Repair your moral standing at once, widen your circle of able advisers, and share power with them—only then might we see whether the situation can be saved.
units.literal: Now urgently cultivate virtue and mend gaps, broadly extend the group of worthies, with them divide responsibilities, still not knowing to obtain relief of what is hoped.

units.zh: 若猶以前事為未工，故復求之於分外，宇宙雖廣，自容何所！
units.en: If you still think you have not failed and reach for still more beyond your proper role, the world is vast—yet where will you find room for yourself?
units.literal: If still taking former affairs as not skillful, therefore again seeking them beyond one's portion, though the cosmos is wide, where is self-accommodation!

units.zh: 知言不必用，或取怨執政，然當情慨所在，正自不能不盡懷極言。
units.en: I know blunt advice may not be heeded and may anger those who govern, but the heart's outrage leaves me no choice but to speak my mind completely.
units.literal: Knowing words need not be used, perhaps incurring resentment of those in power, yet where feeling and indignation lie, just from self must fully in the breast speak to the utmost.

units.zh: 若必親征，未達此旨，果行者，愚智所不解也。
units.en: If you insist on taking the field in person without grasping this point, and actually go through with it, neither the dull nor the clever will understand your reasoning.
units.literal: If you must personally campaign, not comprehending this purport, if indeed proceeding, fool and wise do not understand.

units.zh: 願復與眾共之。
units.en: I urge you to deliberate again with the assembly.
units.literal: I wish again to share with the multitude.

units.zh: 復被州符，增運千石，征役兼至，皆以軍期，對之喪氣，罔知所厝。
units.en: Fresh orders from the province demand another thousand shi of grain and simultaneous levies of labor, all on military deadlines. The people are demoralized and do not know where to turn.
units.literal: Again receiving provincial writs, increasing transport a thousand shi, conscript labor arriving together, all with military deadlines; facing it loses breath, not knowing where to place.

units.zh: 自頃年割剝遺黎，刑徒竟路，殆同秦政，惟未加參夷之刑耳，恐勝廣之憂，無復日矣。
units.en: For years the remnant population has been bled white; shackled convicts choke the highways—policy almost as harsh as the Qin, short only of mass executions by kinship. I fear a Chen Sheng and Wu Guang–style uprising may not be far off.
units.literal: Since recent years carving and stripping the surviving black-haired ones, punished convicts filling the road, roughly equal to Qin government, only not yet adding the three-clans extermination punishment; I fear Chen Sheng and Wu Guang's worry, no again day.

units.zh: 時殷浩與桓溫不協，羲之以國家之安在於內外和，因以與浩書以戒之，浩不從。
units.en: Yin Hao and Huan Wen were at odds. Wang Xizhi believed the realm could be secure only if court and frontier remained at peace, so he wrote to admonish Yin Hao, who paid no heed.
units.literal: At the time Yin Hao and Huan Wen were not harmonious; Xizhi took the state's security as lying in inner and outer harmony, and therefore wrote to Hao to warn him; Hao did not follow.

units.zh: 及浩將北伐，羲之以為必敗，以書止之，言甚切至。
units.en: When Yin Hao prepared a northern campaign, Wang Xizhi was convinced it would end in disaster and sent him a letter urging him to desist, in the frankest terms.
units.literal: When Hao was about to conduct a northern expedition, Xizhi thought it would certainly fail, and tried to stop him with a letter; the words were very urgent and thorough.

units.zh: 又與會稽王箋陳浩不宜北伐，並論時事曰：
units.en: He also wrote to the Prince of Kuaiji arguing that Yin Hao must not launch another northern campaign, and commented on the state of the realm:
units.literal: He also sent a note to the Prince of Kuaiji stating Hao should not northern expedition, and discussing the times' affairs saying:

units.zh: 敦嘗謂羲之曰：「汝是吾家佳子弟，當不減阮主簿。」
units.en: Wang Dun once told him, "You are one of the best youths in our clan; you should prove a match for Clerk Ruan."
units.literal: Dun once said to Xizhi, "You are a fine young man of our house; you ought not fall short of Clerk Ruan."

units.zh: 裕亦目羲之與王承、王悅為王氏三少。
units.en: For his part, Ruan Yu named Wang Xizhi, Wang Cheng, and Wang Yue the three outstanding younger men of the Wang family.
units.literal: Yu also regarded Xizhi with Wang Cheng and Wang Yue as the three young men of the Wang clan.

units.zh: 亮臨薨，上疏稱羲之清貴有鑒裁。
units.en: On his deathbed Yu Liang memorialized the throne, commending Wang Xizhi for his integrity, high standing, and sound judgment.
units.literal: When Liang was near death, he submitted a memorial praising Xizhi as pure, noble, and possessed of judgment.

units.zh: 浩遂行果為姚襄所敗。
units.en: Yin Hao went ahead anyway and was routed by Yao Xiang.
units.literal: Hao then proceeded and indeed was defeated by Yao Xiang.

units.zh: 揚州刺史殷浩素雅重之，勸使應命，乃遺羲之書曰：「悠悠者以足下出處足觀政之隆替，如吾等亦謂為然。
units.en: Yin Hao, the Inspector of Yang province, had always held him in high regard and pressed him to accept. Yin wrote to Wang Xizhi: "Gossip holds that whether you serve or withdraw is itself a barometer of good or bad government—and people like me agree.
units.literal: Inspector of Yang Province Yin Hao had long esteemed him and urged him to answer the summons; he then sent Xizhi a letter saying, "The multitude take your taking office or not as sufficient to observe the rise and decline of government; we too consider it so.

units.zh: 帝又怒曰：「爾自作范增，以我為項羽邪！」
units.en: The emperor raged again. "You make yourself Fan Zeng and call me Xiang Yu!"
units.literal: The emperor was angry again and said, "You make yourself Fan Zeng and take me for Xiang Yu!"

units.zh: 珽曰：「項羽人身亦何由可及，但天命不至耳。
units.en: Ting said, "Xiang Yu as a man—who could match him? Only Heaven's mandate never came.
units.literal: Ting said, "Xiang Yu as a man—how could he be reached? Only Heaven's mandate did not arrive.

units.zh: 項羽布衣，率烏合衆，五年而成霸王業。
units.en: Xiang Yu in plain cloth led a rabble army and in five years built a hegemon's realm.
units.literal: Xiang Yu in plain cloth led a rabble host and in five years achieved the hegemon's enterprise.

units.zh: 陛下藉父兄資，財得至此，臣以項羽未易可輕。
units.en: Your Majesty, on your father's and brother's capital, reached only this. I say Xiang Yu is not to be despised lightly.
units.literal: Your Majesty by your father's and elder brother's resources attained only to this; your servant holds that Xiang Yu is not lightly to be despised.

units.zh: 王出鎮京口，勱將隨之藩，范陽張纘時典選舉，勱造纘言別，纘嘉其風采，乃曰：「王生才地，豈可游外府乎？」
units.en: When the prince went out to hold Jiangkou, Mo was to accompany him to the fief; Zhang Zuan of Fanyang then controlled appointments. Mo came to take leave of him, and Zuan, struck by his bearing, said, "A man of your talent and station—how can he be left to wander in an outer princely house?"
units.literal: When the prince went out to hold Jiangkou, Mo was about to follow to the principality; Zhang Zuan of Fanyang then held selection offices; Mo went to bid Zuan farewell; Zuan admired his presence and said: "Master Wang's talent and standing—how can he wander in an outer princely house?"

units.zh: 永泰元年，會稽太守王敬則反，珍國又率衆距之。
units.en: In Yongtai year one, Kuaiji prefect Wang Jingze rebelled; Zhenguo again led troops against him.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Kuaiji prefect Wang Jingze rebelled; Zhenguo again led troops to resist.

units.zh: 敬則平，遷寧朔將軍、青、冀二州刺史，將軍如故。
units.en: When Jingze was pacified, he was made pacifying-the-north general and inspector of Qing and Ji, general as before.
units.literal: When Jingze was pacified, he was made pacifying-the-north general and inspector of Qing and Ji, general as before.

units.zh: 藹子魯連，吳興昭公主外孫，請全生命，亦得遠徙，世祖即位得還。
units.en: Fan Ai's son Lulian, a grandson of Princess Zhao of Wuxing, pleaded for his life and was likewise exiled to a distant place; when Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, he was permitted to return.
units.literal: Fan Ai's son Lulian, grandson of Princess Zhao of Wuxing, pleaded to spare his life; he too was exiled afar; when Shizu ascended the throne he was allowed to return.

units.zh: 八歲，讀沈約集，見回文研銘，從典援筆擬之，便有佳致。
units.en: At eight he read Shen Yue's collected works. Seeing a palindrome study inscription, Congdian took up the brush to match it and at once produced something fine.
units.literal: At eight he read Shen Yue's collected works; seeing a palindrome study inscription, Congdian took up the brush and imitated it, and at once achieved fine effect.

units.zh: 于時濟陽江總、吳國顧野王、陸瓊、從弟瑜、河南褚玠、北地傅縡等，皆以才學之美，晨夕娛侍。
units.en: At that time Jiang Zong of Jiyang, Gu Yewang of Wu, Lu Qiong, his cousin Yu, Chu Jie of Henan, Fu Zai of Beidi, and others, all famed for learning, served the heir morning and evening as literary companions.
units.literal: At that time Jiang Zong of Jiyang, Gu Yewang of Wu, Lu Qiong, his cousin Yu, Chu Jie of Henan, Fu Zai of Beidi, and others, all distinguished for literary talent, served morning and evening as companions.

units.zh: 又數令共野王遞相策問，恆蒙賞激。
units.en: He was often ordered to question Gu Yewang in turn and always won praise and rewards.
units.literal: He was repeatedly ordered to debate in turn with Gu Yewang and always won reward and praise.

units.zh: 成帝初，清河都尉馮逡奏言：「郡承河下流，與兗州東郡分水為界，城郭所居尤卑下，土壤輕脆易傷。
units.en: Early in Emperor Cheng's reign, Qinghe commandant Feng Jun reported: "Our commandery lies in the downstream path and shares watershed boundaries with Yan and Dong. Our settlements are particularly low, with friable soils that are easily damaged.
units.literal: At the start of Emperor Cheng's reign, Qinghe commandant Feng Jun memorialized: "Our commandery receives downstream river flow, sharing water boundaries with Yan and Dong commanderies; our city sites are especially low, and soil is light and fragile, easily damaged.
